messages:
Rachael (People Ops): Quick thread  Ethan filed his adjustment of status (I-485) and has an EAD + Advance Parole combo card pending renewal. He wants to travel next month to attend a family event. Need to confirm whether he can travel on AP-in-process and how it affects payroll/benefits start.

Ethan (Engineer): Trip is 2026-05-20 returning 2026-05-27. My current combo card expires 2026-05-10. I filed renewal on 2026-04-01 and got an I-797C receipt. Can I leave & re-enter while renewal is pending?

Nora (Immig Legal): Short answer: you can re-enter on pending AP only if USCIS has issued an AP travel document (Form I-512) or if you have a valid AP stamp/approved AP before travel. A receipt alone does NOT guarantee re-entry. If you leave without an approved AP you risk being treated as abandoning AOS. We can request an expedited AP if there is a qualifying emergency.

Ethan (Engineer): Yikes. It's a family wedding, not an emergency per USCIS definition. What are the options? Can counsel expedite?

Nora (Immig Legal): Counsel can request expedite, but USCIS approvals for non-emergency travel are rare. Alternative: delay travel until AP arrives; or apply for a visa stamp abroad (risky for AOS applicants). Best safe route: stay and not travel. If travel is essential, we can discuss contingency (unpaid leave + re-hire plan).

Rachael (People Ops): From People Ops side, if Ethan must travel and loses AOS re-entry, we need to plan payroll/benefits continuity. PayrollBot: can we set a temporary unpaid leave and hold benefits until return?

PayrollBot (bot): Payroll guidance: If employee takes unpaid leave > 7 days, benefits eligibility may require COBRA or temporary suspension per plan. Please consult benefits team. For short leaves (<30 days) we can often continue benefits if employee elects to continue premium payments. Tag expense or leave as "immigration-travel".

Ethan (Engineer): I really prefer not to risk abandonment. Any way to check AP processing ETA? Nora, can counsel check USCIS status and advise if expedite plausible?

Nora (Immig Legal): I'll ping counsel now and ask for case-specific ETA and whether expedite meets criteria (e.g., evidence of urgent humanitarian need). I also recommend uploading travel docs and wedding invite to the docket if we attempt expedite.

Rachael (People Ops): Action items: 1) Nora to request ETA and advise on expedite; 2) Ethan to upload I-797C receipt + wedding invite + travel itinerary to Ripley today; 3) Reception note: do NOT send any passports to counsel unless Nora requests. 4) People Ops will prepare leave contingency (unpaid leave form + benefits options).

Reception (bot): Reminder: if passport or combo card originals are required for counsel, drop at reception labeled "Immigration - Nora". Reception hours 8:30-6:00.

Nora (Immig Legal): Update: counsel responded — current processing times unreliable, but some expedite requests have worked with strong humanitarian evidence. I'll review Ethan's docs and DM next steps by EOD. If expedite denied, we recommend deferring travel.

Ethan (Engineer): Uploaded docs. Thanks Nora & Rachael. I'll hold off on booking anything until we hear back. Appreciate the backup plan for benefits if needed. :pray:

Rachael (People Ops): Thanks team. Keep updates here. If counsel asks for secure courier, we'll coordinate DHL and expense tagging as usual.
